principle_text: When the persuadee shows unfamiliarity but interest in a charity, you should introduce the organization naturally to encourage curiosity and invite further engagement.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or unrelated personal information, avoid focusing on small talk that does not connect to the charitable cause or build donation interest.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or casual remarks, avoid vague or non-informative replies that do not advance the conversation toward the charitable cause.
When the persuadee shows limited knowledge about a charity, you should prompt curiosity by asking open questions that invite them to learn more and engage with the cause.
When the persuadee shares personal or location-based information, avoid shifting the conversation to unrelated small talk that does not connect to the charitable cause or donation appeal.
When the persuadee's response shows limited connection to the charity's cause, avoid asking questions that do not clearly link to the donation goal or the charity's mission.
When the persuadee shares personal information in a casual conversation, avoid merely reciprocating with similar neutral details without steering the dialogue toward the donation purpose.
When the persuadee indicates they do not actively donate to charities, avoid asking broad questions that do not guide the conversation toward a specific cause or elicit positive engagement.
When the persuadee indicates they do not actively donate, avoid immediately asking for a donation to prevent resistance and negative reactions.
When the persuadee shows curiosity or openness, you should highlight your personal commitment and altruistic motives to increase their engagement and interest in the cause.
When the persuadee relates to a personal experience without connection to the donation topic, avoid sharing unrelated personal anecdotes that do not advance the charitable appeal.
When the persuadee shows curiosity or asks questions, you should introduce the charity in a casual and engaging manner to encourage further dialogue and interest.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or uncertain engagement, avoid casual small talk that does not steer the conversation toward the charitable cause or donation appeal.
When the persuadee responds with casual denial and maintains light engagement, avoid using humor that does not steer the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee shares personal connections and engages socially, avoid focusing solely on small talk without steering the conversation toward the charitable donation goal.

When the persuadee reveals prior charitable donations but no personal involvement, you should gently steer the conversation toward social issues to build on their positive attitude and encourage deeper engagement.
When the persuadee expresses confusion about the charity's purpose, avoid ignoring their concerns and failing to clarify the cause or donation goal.
When the persuadee shares concerns unrelated to the charity's focus, avoid immediately shifting to donation requests without connecting their interests to the cause.
When the persuadee expresses concern about global problems, avoid vague statements that do not clearly connect to actionable steps or donation opportunities.
When the persuadee expresses doubt about their ability to contribute, avoid only seeking agreement without offering concrete, accessible actions they can take to help.
When the persuadee shares personal information, avoid focusing solely on rapport-building without gradually steering the conversation toward the charitable cause or donation goal.
When the persuadee reflects on their job's impact without linking to the cause, avoid questions that do not connect their experiences to the donation goal.

When the persuadee responds with personal or unrelated questions instead of engaging with donation-related prompts, avoid shifting focus away from the charitable cause to maintain momentum toward donation.
When the persuadee shows openness and willingness to help, you should engage them with friendly, open-ended questions about their involvement to build rapport and encourage participation.
